items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I don't want you to come in here and try to sound like Freddie Hubbard or anybody else, sound like you, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah. I went backstage and introduced myself. That was awful nervy, you know. Cootie was sitting there practicing and Freddie Jenkins was sitting there practicing. I remember I still could see the book, they had a little band book for band players, exercises for band musicians. And I was so surprised to see jazz musicians practicing. And

naturally, Freddie is going through all kinds of technical exercises, double tongue and (humming). And Cootie is playing very solid, straight-ahead, you know how he plays, he's got the greatest time feel in the world, I think. And even when I was in Benny Goodman's band, I had a very bad period there, I never used to beat my foot. I used to dance when I played, you know, my feet would hop around. And Clark does that, he drives me crazy, his feet keep dancing around.

And Benny saw that one time and he looked at it and he laughed, he would point out my feet. Everytime he would look up he'd laugh. And he got me in such a state that I couldn't play, I couldn't keep time. And I was seriously considering going to a psychiatrist, I was getting desperate. And Cootie finally decided to take over, he was always giving me advice, being my elder. We roomed together a lot on the road, and Cootie showed me how he was -- Cootie would keep both feet like he was marching, you know. Left foot…
